section_summary: This section contains FBI examinations of Japanese consular and related bank accounts, followed by inquiries into a Delaware-incorporated company reportedly associated with a proposed Japanese bond lottery in China. It also covers Japanese gold shipments and reserves, requests to return Japanese bonds and insurance funds, and reports on Japan’s 1941–42 budget. The section ends partway through a detailed budget report.

subfiles.title: Japanese Consulate General special account at Chase National Bank
subfiles.about: Reviews October 1940 deposits and checks in the Japanese Consulate General’s special account.
subfiles.summary: The report lists deposits and withdrawals through October 15, identifies a payment to the Japan Institute, and notes related Showa Tsusho accounts. Investigators planned further examinations of the consular and company accounts.

subfiles.title: Japanese funds: consular accounts and Japanese bank accounts
subfiles.about: Examines September 1940 consular checks, account balances and deposits, and Japanese accounts at National City Bank.
subfiles.summary: Agents inspected signature cards and cancelled checks for the consulate’s regular and special Chase accounts, identifying consular signatories and cashier K. Hoshide. The report tabulates transactions and balances from June through September, lists related accounts, and identifies Japanese banks and firms with National City Bank accounts. Further monthly account reviews were planned.

subfiles.title: Credit to Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha for flour exports to China
subfiles.about: Points to investigation reports concerning Export-Import Bank credit for flour purchases.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references two reports on proposed credit to buy 375,000 barrels of flour for relief in China.

subfiles.title: Mitsubishi Company credit for American flour exports
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Points to a telephone memorandum on credit for American flour exports to China.
subfiles.summary: References a conversation between Fred Mallon and Hamilton about extending credit to Mitsubishi.

subfiles.title: Investigation of the International Finance and Exchange Company
subfiles.about: Investigates the company’s Delaware incorporation, activity, and officers.
subfiles.summary: An inquiry in Wilmington found the company retained a resident agent and had some activity, although its 1939 operations in China were reported inactive. The report lists incorporators, 1936 and 1940 officers and directors, and a 1940 affidavit about its financial difficulties.

subfiles.title: Request to investigate proposed Japanese bond lottery
subfiles.about: Requests investigation of an American-incorporated company reportedly planning a Japanese bond lottery in China.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum cites a Tokyo report of a proposed bond scheme under the company’s name. It seeks evidence of the company’s current status and bona fides to guide possible Department action.

subfiles.title: Passport records of company directors Lorenzen and Young
subfiles.about: Summarizes passport files for two American directors of the International Finance and Exchange Company.
subfiles.summary: The report traces Max Lorenzen’s and Herman Young’s citizenship, families, residences, travel, and business activities, mainly in Tientsin. It supplements the preceding corporate investigation.

subfiles.title: Status of the International Finance and Exchange Company in Tientsin
subfiles.about: Reports directors’ and a former adviser’s statements about the proposed bond scheme.
subfiles.summary: Young and Lorenzen denied knowledge of the scheme and said they were resigning; Fox said the Tientsin office appeared inactive.

subfiles.title: Return of Japanese dollar bonds to Japan
subfiles.about: Records an ITT representative’s report that its Japanese affiliate urgently wanted its remaining dollar bonds returned.
subfiles.summary: Frank Page said the affiliate pressed for an earlier sailing and a Japanese vessel to return bonds held by ITT. He offered no interpretation of the request.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of memorandum on Tokyo Fire and Marine Insurance Company
subfiles.about: Forwards confidential information about withdrawal of the company’s U.S. cash reserves.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a memorandum reporting instructions to send U.S. reserves to Tokyo promptly.
keywords: Tokyo Fire and Marine Insurance Company

subfiles.title: Tokyo Fire and Marine Insurance Company
subfiles.about: Describes the company’s orders to close U.S. branches and remit cash reserves.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reports about $12 million in reserves and quotes urgent December 1940 requests from Tokyo for their remittance.

subfiles.title: Cover note on estimated Japanese monetary gold stock
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Recommends sending the new Japanese gold study to the Embassy in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Suggests seeking the Embassy’s comments and corrections on the study.

subfiles.title: Estimated Monetary Gold Stock of Japan
subfiles.from: Luthringer, Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Estimates Japan’s gold reserves and explains exports and acquisitions from 1937 through December 15, 1940.
subfiles.summary: The study estimates 1940 gold exports at about $74 million, largely covered by newly mined gold, and rejects the unsupported suggestion that recent exports consisted of German-acquired gold. It discusses uncertainty in production estimates and compares its reserve estimate with the Treasury Department’s. A final table gives annual changes in Japan’s monetary gold stock.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese gold stock study to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends the gold stock memorandum and invites Embassy comments.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the study for confidential review alongside a January 1940 memorandum.

subfiles.title: Comments on FBI gold shipment reporting
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Comments on the usefulness and timing of FBI reports about gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: The writer considers the shipment information late and suggests obtaining it promptly from Treasury or the Federal Reserve.

subfiles.title: Japanese gold shipments to San Francisco in November 1940
subfiles.about: Reports two Japanese gold imports and transfer of their proceeds to New York.
subfiles.summary: Details two November shipments totaling over 178,000 fine ounces and subsequent bank transfers for Yokohama Specie Bank.

subfiles.title: Japanese payment for French merchandise
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram concerning currency and timing of Japanese payments for French goods.
subfiles.summary: Notes French preference for prompt dollar or yen payment and Japanese resistance to immediate currency conversion.

subfiles.title: Japanese bonds and National City Bank matter
subfiles.about: Points to an Embassy telegram about withdrawing bank funds or buying Japanese national bonds.
subfiles.summary: References a precautionary message sent after companies approached the Embassy.

subfiles.title: International Finance and Exchange Company, Incorporated
subfiles.from: J. K. Caldwell, American Consul General, Tientsin
subfiles.about: Confirms the company’s American directors’ denial of involvement in the proposed bond lottery.
subfiles.summary: Caldwell reports the company inactive in Tientsin since 1939, says its two local directors intend to resign, and encloses an interview with former adviser Charles Fox.

subfiles.title: Interview with Charles J. Fox about the International Finance and Exchange Company
subfiles.about: Records the former legal adviser’s account of the company’s ownership, offices, and lottery proposal.
subfiles.summary: Fox described Lorenzen and Young as nominal directors for a mainly Japanese enterprise. He said he had discouraged a premium lottery in 1935, the company later failed to pay Tientsin rent, and he knew of no current local business.

subfiles.title: Japanese government estimates, fiscal year 1941–42
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith-Hutton, U.S. Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japan’s proposed general budget, naval allocation, revenue, and expected military expenditure.
subfiles.summary: The Cabinet’s proposed general account totals about ¥6.863 billion, roughly ¥1 billion above the prior year, with ¥1.241 billion for the Navy. The report anticipates that extraordinary military expenses will raise overall spending substantially.

subfiles.title: Dollar Politics
subfiles.from: A. C. Frost, American Consul General, Barcelona
subfiles.about: Forwards a translation of a Spanish newspaper article alleging political motives behind U.S. financial policy.
subfiles.summary: Frost describes an article alleging that U.S. loan offers to Japan had political conditions and extending similar claims to French and British funds.

subfiles.title: Finances, A Political Weapon
subfiles.about: Presents claims that U.S. loans and control of foreign funds served political aims.
subfiles.summary: The article attributes to Japan’s foreign minister a claim that U.S. loans were conditioned on changes in Japanese policy in China. It also alleges U.S. plans to use or seize French and British assets.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Barcelona despatch on dollar politics
subfiles.about: Forwards the Barcelona despatch and its article on financial policy.
subfiles.summary: Sends a copy of Frost’s despatch concerning “Finances, A Political Weapon.”

subfiles.title: Japan’s Gold Position
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Revises estimates of Japan’s gold holdings using final 1940 shipment figures.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reports 1940 gold shipments of 69,648 kilograms, roughly half the 1939 volume and value. Allowing for production, collections, consumption, and exports, it estimates 74,647 kilograms, equivalent to about $86 million, on hand at the start of 1941.

subfiles.title: Cover despatch for National Budget for Japan, 1941–42 Fiscal Year
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Submits the commercial attaché’s detailed report on Japan’s national budget.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Report No. 185 and suggests sharing it with the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.

subfiles.title: National Budget for Japan, 1941–42 Fiscal Year: enclosure title page
subfiles.about: Identifies the enclosed budget report.
subfiles.summary: Cover page for Commercial Attaché Report No. 185.

subfiles.title: National Budget for Japan, 1941–42 Fiscal Year
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s 1941–42 appropriations, borrowing, taxes, and departmental spending.
subfiles.summary: The report describes a record budget dominated by military expenditure and substantial bond financing, comparing it with earlier appropriations and actual bond issues. It gives detailed tables of revenue, extraordinary military accounts, taxes, and spending by department, then reproduces the budget promulgation order and the Finance Ministry’s explanation of its wartime priorities. The itemized expenditure tables continue beyond page 239.
